report:
The scoped counterexample is sound for every n≥2, subject to one harmless wording correction concerning the extended total current on the blowup. The complete supplied R, including its expressly retained foundations, is used as the task grant. Historical review assertions supply no additional authority. R and its retained foundations are excluded from the external-premise array; the task authorization is recorded separately without an external-premise index.

For the radial construction, put s=|z|² and q=Q′. The complex Hessian matrix is (q/s)I+(Q″−q)z̄zᵀ/s². Its tangential eigenvalues are q/s, with multiplicity n−1, and its radial eigenvalue is Q″/s. Positivity therefore follows from Q′≥0 and Q″≥0. The joins at −1 and −log 2 match both values and derivatives. The tangent-line inequality handles the middle interval; on L≥1, differentiation of L^(2/3)/(1+e^L) verifies the asserted decreasing bound and hence Q′(−L)>Q₀′(−L). Thus w≤0, equals zero outside the indicated ball, and has precisely the pole p. Local bounded-above psh extension establishes the weight at that pole, and the exterior equality gives the global projective gluing.

Polar integration of the Hessian determinant, with the angular normalization fixed by FS volume one, gives d(q^n). Polarizing the determinant gives exactly d(q^k q₀^(n−k)), where q₀=Q₀′. These identities extend across the joins by decreasing smooth convex approximation and [Bedford–Taylor continuity](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf), premise 0. The distribution functions are continuous at both joins, so neither interface carries mass. Every mixed distribution starts at zero and ends at one. In particular, the top measure on the complement of p has mass one; the nonpluripolar extension therefore has full probability mass. This conclusion does not depend on an inference from zero Lelong number.

On the inner region, q=3⁻¹L⁻²ᐟ³ and Q″=(2/9)L⁻⁵ᐟ³. The top radial density is (2n/3^(n+1))L^(−2n/3−1)dL. Multiplication by |w|=O(1+L^(1/3)) gives an integrable energy tail O(L^(−(2n+2)/3)dL). For k<n, the mixed derivative has the extra exponential factor e^(−(n−k)L), up to polynomial factors. All energy summands are consequently absolutely finite.

The truncation argument also checks the actual extended energy. Its total weight is max(Q,Q₀−j), and L_j≈j³. For the kth mixed product, its boundary atom is q(−L_j)^k q₀(−L_j)^(n−k)−q₀(−L_j)^n. Multiplying by the boundary value −j gives a vanishing contribution: the top bound is O(j^(1−2n)), and lower terms decay exponentially. The capped interior contributes O(j e^(−nL_j)); the omitted untruncated tails tend to zero by the integrability just established. Hence E(max(w,−j)) decreases to the displayed finite energy, proving w∈E¹. The reference-volume summand is strictly negative, so E(w)<0.

The exact inner probability density is f=(2/3^(n+1))e^(nL)(1+e^(−L))^(n+1)L^(−2n/3−1). This verifies equation (5). Its positive entropy tail has leading integrability requirement ∫L^(−2n/3)dL<∞, which holds precisely for the integer dimensions n≥2 considered here. The middle region has zero top density, the exterior density is one, and the interfaces have no singular mass. The negative part is bounded using f log f≥−1/e against the probability reference. Thus the initial probability entropy is genuinely finite. The analogous n=1 tail diverges.

The blowup geometry is actual. On a projective chart Z_j≠0 meeting H, with j≥1, write x=Z₀/Z_j. The section ideal is (x,τ). In the x-chart of its blowup, division by x leaves a unit among the sections; in the τ-chart, division by τ leaves the section corresponding to τZ_j equal to a unit. Off the center a generator is already a unit. Thus the divided sections globally generate L over A¹ and define g with L=g*O(1), using premises 2–3. Over the complementary time chart the blowup and bundle are the trivial product. This proves relative generation, semiampleness and nefness over the entire compactified base. The time action lifts because the center is invariant.

In the x-chart, τ=xu, so the central divisor is F₀+E with both multiplicities one. The Jacobian dx∧dτ=x dx∧du gives relative canonical coefficient one on E; the strict component has coefficient zero. The conormal bundle is O_H(−1)⊕O_H, and the quotient convention identifies O_E(1) with O(−E)|E. In the universal quotient sequence, the kernel has first Chern class −h−ξ, giving ξ²+hξ=0. Fiber integration gives q_*ξ=1. Consequently L|F₀ is trivial and ∫E(h+ξ)^n=1. Also T^nE=0 and T^(n+1−r)E^r=−1 for 2≤r≤n+1, yielding (T−E)^(n+1)=−n.

The retained NA model formulas apply with their precise positivity hypotheses. If using the supplied MPWN formulas stated for obstacles ≥1, translate by 2: D′=2(F₀+E)−E=2F₀+E and φ′=φ+2≥1. The class T+D′ is big and nef, its positive products equal its ordinary intersections, and the translation leaves central component intersections unchanged. Undoing the translation gives E^NA(φ)=−n/(n+1). The multiplicity-weighted component masses are 0 and 1. The exceptional component restricts to ord_H, and (κ+1−b)/b=1 there. Therefore MA^NA(φ)=δ_ord_H and H^NA(φ)=1.

The ideal computation establishes φ(v)=−min(v(H),1) on the original full carrier. Off H the divisor generator is a unit. At a center on H, some Z_j with j≥1 supplies the time generator τ. This includes supported semivaluations with v(H)=+∞, where the value is −1. No restriction to function-field valuations or replacement of the supported carrier occurs.

Equation (9) defines a smooth, bounded-slice, strongly continuous actual ray. On the punctured family its total current is g*ω_FS and its (n+1)st power vanishes. Canonicality can also be checked directly: along the holomorphic curves on which g is constant, the difference between any subgeodesic competitor and a is subharmonic with nonpositive boundary values. The maximum principle makes that difference nonpositive on every finite annulus. The divided-section compatibility gives the usual datum φ, including its sign. Energy affinity and the initial derivative −∫r²/(1+r²)ω^n=−n/(n+1) give E(a_t)=−nt/(n+1). The actual-ray energy-defect criterion in R therefore proves a=r(0,φ).

The wording correction is that, across the exceptional divisor, the extended pulled-back total current is [E]+g*ω_FS. The residual current after removal of [E] is g*ω_FS. The manuscript's statement about the current on the blowup should specify this removal. The HCMA equation is imposed on the punctured family, where [E] disappears, and the datum calculation already retains the exceptional divisor. Every dependent inference remains valid.

The entropy calibration is correct: transporting x=e^(−t)r²/(1+e^(−t)r²) gives probability density n x^(n−1)dx and log relative density t+(n+1)log(x+e^(−t)(1−x)). Since log x≤log(x+e^(−t)(1−x))≤0 and its transported average lower bound is −1/n, equation (11), finiteness at every finite time, and slope one follow with the specified squared-log time.

The absolute endpoint proof works at zero mass. Poincaré–Lelong gives ω+dd^c w_H=[H]. Outside H this current vanishes, so every positive-degree nonpluripolar product vanishes. For any proper competitor h≤w_H+C, subtracting the local divisor logarithm produces a psh function locally bounded above near H. [Demailly's extension theorem](https://www.ime.usp.br/~cordaro/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Jean-Pierre-Demailly-Complex-Analytic-and-Differential-Geometry-1.pdf), premise 1, gives a positive residual current in the zero class. Its positive trace measure has total mass zero, hence the current vanishes. Compact connectedness then gives h=w_H+C′. With the additional ceiling h≤0, C′≤0. Since w_H is admissible for every C≥0, P_ω(w_H+C,0)=w_H and P_ω[w_H]=w_H. No positive-mass envelope theorem is invoked here.

The stationary unbounded ray is canonical: bounded truncations give constant canonical segments, and the retained decreasing finite-energy construction gives the constant segment w. At a generic Gauss divisor over p, ρ is a fixed multiple of log|s|² plus a bounded term; the singular weight is consequently O(t^(1/3)) and has logarithm-square coefficient zero. At every other generic center it is locally bounded. Divisorial determination in R extends these coefficients to the usual datum zero on the entire carrier. Its energy defect vanishes, so r(w,0)=w. Adding −t gives usual datum −1 and energy slope −1, proving r(w,−1)=w−t.

All hypotheses for R's order and existence statements are now established: w∈E¹, φ∈E¹,NA, w≤0, and −1≤φ≤0 on the full carrier. They give the actual maximal ray b and all inequalities (12). At each point outside p, b_t is a finite convex function bounded above on the whole half-line, hence is nonincreasing. At p it is always −∞. The decreasing-limit theorem, premise 4, shows that the limit is either proper ω-psh or identically −∞. Under the explicit assumption of a proper limit h, the inequalities imply h≤w_H and h≤w. The independently proved rigidity gives h=w_H+C′, but h(p)=C′ is finite while w(p)=−∞. Thus that assumption is impossible, and χ_b(0)≡−∞.

Finally, R's ordered d₁ identity and maximal energy formula give d₁(a_t,b_t)=E(a_t)−E(b_t)=−E(w), including t=0. Both distances and energies use the stated normalization. Maximality, the verified finite initial entropy and H^NA(φ)=1 place b in R's finite branch, giving entropy slope one. R's full body, equation (20), already gives finite entropy at every finite time in this situation. The manuscript's additional convexity inference is valid as well: a finite asymptotic entropy limit supplies finite-entropy times arbitrarily far out, and the retained [BDL Theorem 4.7](https://msp.org/gt/2017/21-5/gt-v21-n5-p08-s.pdf) bounds the extended Mabuchi functional between its finite endpoint values. Its contracted energies are finite on E¹. The substitution u/(2π) preserves the currents and probability entropy, so this application has the correct operator convention.

The conclusion is exactly the stated obstruction to absolute smooth-background zero-endpoint invariance. It establishes neither full P19.2 nonexistence nor failure of envelopes adapted to a singular start. No singularity metric is assigned to the identically −∞ level, and neither zero raw endpoint mass is normalized into a probability.

passages.statement: Let Ω⊂C^N be open and 1≤k≤N. For each i=1,…,k, let u_{i,j} be a decreasing sequence of locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions converging pointwise to a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function u_i. Then dd^c u_{1,j}∧⋯∧dd^c u_{k,j} converges weakly to dd^c u_1∧⋯∧dd^c u_k. Locally bounded mixed Bedford–Taylor products are symmetric and multilinear. These statements hold under any fixed positive rescaling of dd^c. Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2.

For each i=1,…,k, let u_{i,j} be a decreasing sequence of locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions converging pointwise to a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function u_i. Then dd^c u_{1,j}∧⋯∧dd^c u_{k,j} converges weakly to dd^c u_1∧⋯∧dd^c u_k. Locally bounded mixed Bedford–Taylor products are symmetric and multilinear. These statements hold under any fixed positive rescaling of dd^c. Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2.

Let M be a complex manifold, A⊂M a closed pluripolar set, and v∈PSH(M∖A) locally bounded above near every point of A. Then v has a unique plurisubharmonic extension to M. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter I, Theorem 5.24.

passages.statement: Let Y be a smooth closed complex algebraic subvariety of positive codimension in a smooth complex algebraic variety Z, with ideal sheaf I. For π:Bl_Y Z→Z and exceptional divisor E, the blowup and E are smooth, π is an isomorphism away from Y, I·O_{Bl_Y Z}=O_{Bl_Y Z}(−E), and E is canonically P_Y(I/I²) in the quotient Proj(Sym) convention, with O_E(1)=O_{Bl_Y Z}(−E)|_E. The Stacks Project, Lemmas 37.17.3 and 31.33.4.

For a scheme S and a finite locally free sheaf V, P_S(V)=Proj_S(Sym V) represents invertible quotients of pullbacks of V and carries the universal surjection q*V→O_{P_S(V)}(1). In particular, a line bundle L on a complex scheme T generated by n+1 global sections defines a morphism g:T→P^n_C with g*O(1)≅L. The Stacks Project, Section 27.21 and Example 27.21.2.
passages.quote: the set of $\mathcal{O}_T$-module quotients of $f^*\mathcal{E}$ which are locally free of rank $1$.

passages.statement: For an open set Ω⊂C^N, a pointwise decreasing sequence of plurisubharmonic functions has a plurisubharmonic limit when the identically −∞ function is allowed. Under the convention excluding that function, on each connected component the limit is either plurisubharmonic or identically −∞. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter I, Theorem 5.4.
